runs.content:
## Week of 2026-11-26

> Generated by `podcast-recommender` (Thursday run, two days after the Tuesday 11-24 run). Three picks this week: a health pick was dropped because the best result (the Sherzais' Brain Health Revolution) duplicates last week's "Your Brain On", and the other longevity results were weak or sponsor-led. Facts come from web search results; episode dates not individually verified.

### Think Like A Game Designer
Host: Justin Gary (designer of Ascension, CEO of Stone Blade Entertainment)
Why for Fred: Fred has just finished Designer Notes with Sid Meier and Jake Solomon, and is building his own autobattler. This show interviews designers about process. Guests include Ben Brode (Hearthstone), Jonathan Tweet (D&D 3rd Edition) and Soren Johnson, the Designer Notes host. Gary comes from card and deckbuilder games, which suits autobattler economy and drafting questions.
Format: Long-form interview, ~60 min
Sample episode to start with: The Ben Brode episode (Hearthstone design), or the Soren Johnson episode as a bridge from Designer Notes
Links: [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/podcast/id1450200089)

---

### Kepler Trust Intelligence Podcast
Host: Kepler Partners research team (Trust Issues interviews by Jo Groves and colleagues)
Why for Fred: Fund managers explain how they run UK-listed investment trusts. A 2026 special edition covers investing in Europe, and Fidelity European Trust's Marcel Stötzel talks about the outlook for European equities. It fills a gap next to Behind the Balance Sheet and The Value Perspective: the closed-end trust structure, discounts, and UK/European income managers.
Format: Fund manager interviews ("Trust Issues") plus a monthly "Market Matters" roundup, ~20–40 min
Sample episode to start with: The 2026 special edition on investing in Europe, or the Fidelity European Trust episode with Marcel Stötzel
Links: [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/kepler-trust-intelligence-podcast/id1628343255) · [Podbean](https://keplertrustintelligence.podbean.com/)

---

### Sharp Tech with Ben Thompson
Host: Ben Thompson (Stratechery) and Andrew Sharp
Why for Fred: Thompson's aggregation theory and his analysis of AI economics are the strategy counterpart to the Dwarkesh episodes Fred has finished on compute and scaling. Each episode tests the AI race in terms of business models: who captures value, advertising against subscriptions, and what inference costs do to margins. That feeds directly into Fred's AI holdings (Meta, Microsoft, Google, Oracle). Caveat: full episodes need a Stratechery Plus subscription, and the free feed carries previews.
Format: Weekly two-host analysis with listener questions, ~60–90 min
Sample episode to start with: The March 2025 episode recorded after Thompson's Sam Altman interview (an AI symposium)
Links: [stratechery.com](https://stratechery.com/)

---

runs.content:
## Week of 2026-11-24

> Generated by `podcast-recommender` scheduled task (run on Tuesday; no run for Thu 2026-11-19 is recorded). Recent episodes checked on Apple Podcasts where listed; Apple omits years, so 2026 is inferred from the listing order. The host of Money Maze and the Shell Game Season 2 premise come from web search results.

### Shell Game
Host: Evan Ratliff
Why for Fred: Season 2 follows Ratliff building a real company, HurumoAI, staffed by AI agents, and what happens when it hires its first human. It joins two of Fred's threads: serialised reporting (Kill List, The Conti Files) and AI's effect on work (AI & I, the Growth Podcast episode on Claude loops). The premise is also close to the satire in The Optimised Jungle. Season 3 is a short miniseries on AI-generated "slop".
Format: Serialised narrative documentary, three seasons, ~40–50 min for the recent episodes
Sample episode to start with: Season 2, Episode 1 (Nov 2025; serialised, so play in order), or "Into the Slop" (Season 3, Episode 1) for something shorter
Links: [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/id1753117762) · [Omny](https://omny.fm/shows/shell-game)

---

### Money Maze Podcast
Host: Simon Brewer
Why for Fred: Brewer talks to allocators, fund founders and CEOs about process and capital cycles, so it's a natural companion to Capital Allocators and Behind the Balance Sheet. Recent episodes cover the credit cycle with Victor Khosla of Strategic Value Partners, and fraud and due diligence in alternatives with Albourne's John Claisse. Joel Greenblatt's London Value Investor Conference conversation suits the value side. Caveat: a separate "Curated" series is funded by the firms it features.
Format: Long-form interview, fortnightly, ~45–65 min
Sample episode to start with: "The Quiet Before the Credit Storm?" with Victor Khosla (Nov 2026)
Links: [moneymazepodcast.com](https://moneymazepodcast.com/) · [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/id1504477769)

---

### Your Brain On
Host: Drs Ayesha and Dean Sherzai (neurologists)
Why for Fred: Each episode takes one factor and asks what the evidence says it does to the brain, which fits Fred's dementia-prevention priority directly. The 2026 run includes vascular dementia, memory testing, the MIND diet and testosterone, the last two especially relevant to a man of about 50. Caveat: the newest episode listed is from 15 July, so treat it as a back catalogue between seasons.
Format: Single-topic deep dives with guests, released in seasons, ~30–100 min
Sample episode to start with: "Your Brain On... Vascular Dementia" (Feb 2026), then "Your Brain On... the MIND Diet" (Jun 2026)
Links: [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/id1730984252)

---

### The Comedian's Comedian Podcast
Host: Stuart Goldsmith
Why for Fred: A working stand-up interviews other comedians about how material gets written, tested and fixed. That's useful craft listening for The Optimised Jungle, and earlier writing picks (Scriptnotes, Writing Excuses) didn't cover comedy specifically. It follows on from the Jimmy Carr episode of What Now? that Fred finished. The archive is deep, at 585 listed episodes, with older interviews reissued as "ComCompendium".
Format: Long-form interview, roughly weekly, ~60–95 min
Sample episode to start with: "Elf Lyons Returns" or "Paul Foot Returns" (both Oct 2026)
Links: [Acast](https://shows.acast.com/thecomedianscomedianpodcast) · [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/id513734888)

---
